questions.text: Four fair six-sided dice are rolled. The probability that the sum of the results being 22 is [latex]\frac{X}{1296}[/latex]. The value of X is _________
questions.solution:
Let each die show 6 [latex]-[/latex] [latex]d_i[/latex]. Sum 22 means [latex]d_1+d_2+d_3+d_4=2[/latex] with [latex]d_i\ge0[/latex]: [latex]\binom{2+3}{3}=10[/latex] ways.

Answer: 10

questions.text:
There are 5 bags labelled 1 to 5. All the coins in a given bag have the same weight. Some
bags have coins of weight 10 gm, others have coins of weight 11 gm. I pick 1, 2, 4, 8, 16
coins respectively from bags 1 to 5. Their total weight comes out to 323 gm. Then the product
of the labels of the bags having 11 gm coins is ___.
questions.solution:
If all coins were 10 g: (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16) [latex]\times[/latex] 10 = 310 g. The extra 13 g comes from bags with 11 g coins, each adding 1 g per coin picked: 13 = 1 + 4 + 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bags 1, 3, 4.

Product = 1 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 12

Answer: 12

questions.text:
Consider the directed graph given below.

Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Edges: P [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q, P [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R, R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q, S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R, S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q. P and S have no incoming edges and can come first in either order; R must come before Q.

PSRQ and SPRQ are both valid; PQRS is not (Q before R).

Answer: Both PSRQ and SPRQ are topological orderings

questions.text:
Let G be a graph with n vertices and m edges. What is the tightest upper bound on the
running time of Depth First Search on G, when G is represented as an adjacency matrix?
questions.solution:
With an adjacency matrix, finding the neighbours of a vertex means scanning its whole row of n entries. DFS does this for every vertex: [latex]n\times n=\Theta(n^2)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex]

questions.text: Let G=(V,E) be a directed graph where V is the set of vertices and E the set of edges. Then which one of the following graphs has the same strongly connected components as G ?
questions.solution:
Reversing every edge keeps every cycle (just traversed backwards). If u and v can reach each other in G, they still can in the reversed graph, so the strongly connected components are the same.

The complement graph, the "paths of length [latex]\le[/latex] 2" graph and removing isolated vertices can all change the SCCs.

Answer: [latex]G_2[/latex] with all edges reversed
